name: Question 15
problem: The curve $C$ is the intersection of a surface $S,$ defined by $z=f(x,y),$ with the plane $y=1.$ Given that the point $P(1,1,1)$ lies on $C$, and that ${f}_{x}=2(x+y)-2$, which of the following gives a tangent vector to $C$ at $P?$
worked_solution:
The curve $C$ is the intersection of the surface with the plane $y=1.$ Hence, the slope of the tangent to the curve $C$ at the point $P$ will be given by the partial derivative ${f}_{x}(1,1).$ 

To get the slope, we evaluate the partial derivative ${f}_{x}(x,y)$ at $(1,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(1,1) & =2(1+1)-2=2\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we use the point-slope form of a straight line:

$$
\begin{aligned}z-f(1,1) & ={f}_{x}(1,1)(x-1) \\ z-1 & =2(x-1) \\ z-1 & =2x-2 \\ z & =2x-1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the tangent line to the curve $C$ at $P(1,1,1)$ can be given as the intersection of two planes:

$$
{\begin{aligned}y=1 \\ z=2x-1\end{aligned}
$$

Next, notice that:

- For the plane $y=1,$ a normal vector to the plane is ${n}_{1}=⟨0,1,0⟩.$

- For the plane $z=2x-1$ (or $2x-z-1=0$), a normal vector to the plane is ${n}_{2}=⟨2,0,-1⟩.$

Finally, to find a direction vector for the tangent line, we calculate the cross product of these normal vectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}{n}_{1}\times {n}_{2} & =⟨0,1,0⟩\times ⟨2,0,-1⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =-i-2\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since $-i-2\,k$ is parallel to the tangent line, then $-(-i-2\,k)=i+2\,k$ is also parallel to it.

Question 15
?

The curve C is the intersection of a surface S, defined by z=f(x,y), with the plane y=1. Given that the point P(1,1,1) lies on C, and that fx=2(x+y)−2, which of the following gives a tangent vector to C at P?

a
i−2k
b
2i−2k
c
i+2k
d
−3i+k
e
i+k
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The curve C is the intersection of the surface with the plane y=1. Hence, the slope of the tangent to the curve C at the point P will be given by the partial derivative fx(1,1).

To get the slope, we evaluate the partial derivative fx(x,y) at (1,1):

fx(1,1)=2(1+1)−2=2

Now, we use the point-slope form of a straight line:

z−f(1,1)=fx(1,1)(x−1)z−1=2(x−1)z−1=2x−2z=2x−1

Therefore, the tangent line to the curve C at P(1,1,1) can be given as the intersection of two planes: {y=1z=2x−1

Next, notice that:

  • For the plane y=1, a normal vector to the plane is n1=⟨0,1,0⟩.

  • For the plane z=2x−1 (or 2x−z−1=0), a normal vector to the plane is n2=⟨2,0,−1⟩.

Finally, to find a direction vector for the tangent line, we calculate the cross product of these normal vectors:

n1×n2=⟨0,1,0⟩×⟨2,0,−1⟩=ijk01020−1=−i−2k

Finally, since −i−2k is parallel to the tangent line, then −(−i−2k)=i+2k is also parallel to it.
